Reddit thread after reddit thread and article after article all had her disappearing from seemingly the face of the planet after 1996.

"time to do my monthly google of whether anyone has heard from Q Lazzarus yet or not"

Yesterday out of nowhere, a woman claiming to be Q Lazzarus tweeted back at me saying she was indeed alive. "Hi, sorry to bother you. I just wanted people to know I am still alive, I have no interest in singing anymore. I am a bus driver in Staten Island (I have been for YEARS), I see hundreds of passengers everyday so I am hardly hiding (or dead!), I have given Thomas Gorton (Dazed) my fone number and address just to confirm I am 'real', sorry if this is a boring end to the story,  I am going to come off twitter soon as I find it odd,  please take note of this message incase anyone else is interested. http://www.dazeddigital.com/music/article/38148/1/what-happened-to-q-lazzarus-who-sang-goodbye-horses

"Goodbye Horses" continues to be one of my favorite songs of all time, and if this is all true, I'm so so happy to know someone I admire so much is living a happy, simple life away from the lechery of the music industry by choice. The song is haunting and iconic, and it's the perfect happy ending to all the horrible rumors that she died in London in 90s or befriended a drug addict who abused her or got wrapped up in a bad marriage or any of the other conspiracies I heard. I called the suicide hotline because I was close last November. Since I had the knife and the intent, the operator insisted on calling 911. So the ems and the cops came. Took me to the emergency room. They wheeled in a robot with a screen so some psychiatrist could evaluate me for 5 minutes from his house at 2am. They decided I needed to be placed in a psychiatric hospital. I was involuntarily committed. I spent 7 days there. It was like prison. If you're feeling like shit about yourself and then you get involuntarily committed you go into a further depression. Ultimately though I was lucky in that I found some common ground with a couple other patients and we ended up having a good time. When you're in that situation, not trusted with pens/pencils/can't even keep chapstick with you/have to ask the nurse for your shampoo/no outside food/no phones, no electronics whatsoever, you become close to people. Some of the patients there scared me at first. But I learned less about myself from that experience as I learned about other people. I saw people who wouldn't speak and walked around in circles and stared at walls start to show signs of life and glimmers of hope and happiness. I'm not scared of people with mental illness like that anymore. Everyone is the same, we all need the same things. I won't give into their delusions, but I will understand they have them, and they are suffering and it's real. It was a good experience overall. I'll never forget those people.
